Summary: First tour of the web application: signing in as an administrator, an employee, a manager and a reviewer, and what each can see and do. Shows the document library, search and filters, document details, upload, approvals, shared lists and the organization and permissions pages; features without screens yet are named as still to come.

Choosing how the application looks: the default design, previewing and applying a design on the Appearance page, a colleague with a different design in the same organization, the choice following a person to a new sign-in, the platform administrator's Design catalogue refusing an unsafe file, publishing a sixth design without redeployment and resetting to default.

Everyday work with documents: Uploaded by me and editing details, adding a version, previewing a PDF on the page, restoring an old version, sharing with a colleague, review comments, rejection and sending for review again, a legal hold blocking a deletion request, deletion with a second approver, and the due-soon list.

Administering the organization: employees and roles with the last administrator protected, invitations, join requests, lost-device two-step reset, the audit log and search index, creating a category with review steps and rules and publishing a new rules version, tags, and editing departments, project people and employee details.

How people get in and look after their own account: an administrator allowing join requests, a new colleague asking to join, approval and the invitation email, choosing a password (weak and mismatched passwords refused), a used link refused, a forgotten-password reset, the Google and Microsoft buttons (shown with a test setting; real provider sign-in not yet set up), changing a password with other devices signed out, and turning two-step verification on (QR, recovery codes shown once), signing in with a code, and off.

The new dashboard, now the first page after sign-in: the four figures (documents you can see, reviews waiting, shared with you, storage), the 30-day upload chart, documents by classification, recent documents and the review queue, links from figures to the library, an employee seeing smaller numbers than the administrator because only visible documents are counted, and the same information laid out by three designs (dense grid with due-soon and activity, focused column, dark with welcome banner).

The stack Coolify will run, shown through its one public address on a local copy: web, service and database behind one address, the two health addresses, creating the first organization and administrator with a single command and a one-time link, the five standard designs already published, creating a category and uploading a first document (virus scan off for the first release), inviting a colleague before email is ready (link command, then four email settings), and what is left for the owner: server, domain, verified email, production bucket. Not deployed to a real server.

Files: The DMS on a phone-sized screen (portrait video): the phone layout with a bottom bar and a red badge for waiting reviews, the dashboard with two figures per row, document search with folded filters, opening a document with versions as cards and an on-screen preview, uploading a photo of a delivery receipt (the camera is stood in for by a saved photo) with the fields the category asks for, approving a review from the phone in a full-screen review, the More list, and how to put it on the home screen on Android and iPhone.
